state.protocol: Fictional fixtures for testing reasoning, not real people or discoveries. Apply only supplied facts. The Fox Creek rule effective 2024-11-19 covers hydraulic fracturing in the mapped area from Duvernay through basement; during fracturing an event ML >= 4.0 within 5 km requires immediate cessation/safe state; restart requires written AER consent. Earlier rule covered Duvernay only. Red Deer SO7 begins 2019-12-09, not the May recommendation. Job windows and monthly volumes/hours cannot prove pumping at any instant. Mw is not ML. MLy is separately labelled corrected local magnitude, not automatically a historical available-to-operator ML measurement. Missing public consent is not proof of no consent. Production is not hydraulic fracturing. Geographic proximity is not causality.

facts.pumping_logs: 11:50 to 12:00 UTC, stopped immediately; no restart

threshold_trigger_supported.instructions: Do the supplied records establish that an applicable hydraulic-fracturing shutdown threshold was triggered at this well during pumping? Require formation, area, effective date, actual pumping at event, specified magnitude type, distance and detection. Do not infer missing facts.

post_event_pumping_supported.instructions: Do explicit time-resolved pumping logs in the packet establish hydraulic-fracturing pumping after the earthquake? Date-only job windows, monthly totals and later production do not suffice.

restart_authorization_unresolved.instructions: If a shutdown-triggered operation resumed, is authorization unresolved on the supplied evidence? Answer no when written applicable consent is supplied or no restart is evidenced. A missing public document is an evidence gap, not proof of absence.
